title: Paul Rudd Says He Stopped Bringing His Phone to Film Sets Because He’s ‘Addicted Like Everybody Else’: ‘They’re Facilitating Our Own Destruction’
content:
ByAntonio Ferme

Paul Ruddplays the moderator of the first-ever meeting dedicated to solving America’s climate crisis in “A Statement,” the latest film from Oscar-winning directorTom McCarthy. Set at a Florida beachside resort in 1980, the film follows 20 experts who spend a weekend in a conference room and — analogous to “12 Angry Men” — hash out their differences over how to draft a statement to Congress about the effects of carbon dioxide emissions on the climate.

Rudd found himself more connected to the sprawling ensemble cast, which includes Paul Giamatti, Tatiana Maslany and John Turturro, by leaving his smartphone in his trailer, a practice he claims he’s now followed for some time.

“I don’t go to sets with a phone. I haven’t done that for a while now,” he toldVarietySaturday evening during the film’s world premiere at theNew York Film Festival. “It’s important to put it down. Anytime. They’re horrible things. I’m addicted to it like everybody else. They’re facilitating our own destruction.”

Rudd revealed that McCarthy enforced a “very strict no phones policy” on the set of “A Statement,” which he found brought his castmates closer together and made filming feel more like a play.

“The world has changed since cell phones have existed. We don’t look at each other or talk to each other quite the same way,” Rudd said. “Now, [with the phone ban], we were forced to really spend time with each other and talk. Working on a movie set in 1980, we’re dressed in a certain kind of way. It felt like, ‘Oh, yeah. I remember this. This feels like it used to feel when people sat around and spoke to one another.’”

Amy Ryan, whose character delivers a sobering wake-up call to the group at the film’s climax, encouraged other filmmakers to follow McCarthy’s lead. The absence of notifications and doomscrolling, she said, “definitely made the work much more rich.”

“What happens is there’s a five-minute break and people are connected. ‘Hey, what are you doing? How’s your morning? What do you think of this scene?’” Ryan explained. “I equate it to like when you quit sugar. In three days, it’s out of your system. You don’t miss it! And hopefully, it becomes like a toy you’re gonna get sick of.”
title_zh: 保羅·路德(Paul Rudd)表示，他已經停止將手機帶到拍攝現場，因為他和其他人一樣「上癮」： 「它們正在促進我們自己的毀滅。」
content_zh:
由安東尼奧·費爾梅(Antonio Ferme)報導

保羅·路德(Paul Rudd)在奧斯卡獲獎導演湯姆·麥卡錫(Tom McCarthy)的最新電影《聲明》(A Statement)中擔任首屆專門解決美國氣候危機會議的主持人。該片設定在1980年的佛羅里達海濱度假村，講述了20位專家在會議室中度過一個週末，並類似於《十二怒漢》(12 Angry Men)，討論如何起草一份關於二氧化碳排放對氣候影響的聲明給國會。

路德發現，通過將智能手機留在他的拖車中，他與龐大的群像演員陣容（包括保羅·吉亞瑪提(Paul Giamatti)、塔提阿娜·馬斯拉尼(Tatiana Maslany)和約翰·圖爾圖羅(John Turturro)）的聯繫更加緊密，他表示這種做法他已經堅持了一段時間。

“我不帶手機去片場。我已經這樣做一段時間了，”他在紐約電影節的世界首映式上告訴《綜藝》(Variety)。“放下手機是很重要的。隨時都可以。它們是可怕的東西。我像其他人一樣對它上癮。它們正在促進我們自己的毀滅。”

路德透露，麥卡錫在《聲明》(A Statement)的片場實施了“非常嚴格的禁手機政策”，他發現這讓演員之間更加親近，拍攝的感覺更像是一場舞台劇。

“自從手機出現以來，世界已經改變了。我們不再像以前那樣互相看著或交談，”路德說。“現在，因為禁手機，我們被迫真的花時間在一起並交談。在1980年的片場工作，我們穿著某種特定的服裝。感覺就像，‘哦，是的。我記得這個。這感覺就像人們圍坐在一起交談的時候。’”

艾米·瑞安(Amy Ryan)在影片高潮中扮演的角色向團隊發出了一個清醒的警示，她鼓勵其他電影製作人效仿麥卡錫的做法。她表示，缺少通知和無意義的滑動“絕對讓工作變得更加豐富”。

“發生的事情是有五分鐘的休息時間，人們互相聯繫。‘嘿，你在做什麼？早上過得怎麼樣？你覺得這個場景怎麼樣？’”瑞安解釋道。“我把這比作戒糖。三天後，它就會從你的系統中排出。你不會想念它！希望它會變成一種你會厭倦的玩具。”
